e-7657.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality When the Base of the Exponential is Greater Than One
e-7657.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}4{e}^{x}-5 & >0 \\ 4{e}^{x} & >5 \\ {e}^{x} & >\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x}) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{5}{4}) \\ x & >\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡4.\end{aligned}
$$

e-7703.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality When the Base of the Exponential is Between Zero and One
e-7703.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot {(\frac{3}{4})}^{x}+2 & \ge 12 \\ 5\cdot {(\frac{3}{4})}^{x} & \ge 10 \\ {(\frac{3}{4})}^{x} & \ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{3}{4})}^{x}] & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{4}) & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡4) & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\ln 3 - \ln 4$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

e-7704.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality When the Exponential is Compared to Zero or a Negative Number
e-7704.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot {3}^{8-x}+12 & >0 \\ 4\cdot {3}^{8-x} & >-12 \\ {3}^{8-x} & >-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Because a power of a positive number is always greater than $0,$ we must have

$$
3^{8-x} > 0
$$

for all values of $x.$

Therefore, the inequality $3^{8-x} > -3$ is satisfied for all real values of $x.$

e-7660.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality with Exponential Functions on Both Sides
e-7660.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot {5}^{x} & <{7}^{3-x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot {5}^{x}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{3-x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{3-x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & <(3-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & <3\operatorname{ln}⁡7-x\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡5+x\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & <3\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7) & <3\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ x & <\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Subtract 1 and divide by 2 to get e^{x-2}<1. Taking natural logarithms preserves the inequality, giving x-2<0, so x<2.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}2{e}^{x-2}+1 & <3 \\ 2{e}^{x-2} & <2 \\ {e}^{x-2} & <1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-2}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\ x-2 & <0 \\ x & <2.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Divide by 2 to get (0.7)^{x+9}≥2. Taking logarithms gives (x+9)ln(0.7)≥ln(2). Since ln(0.7)<0, division reverses the inequality, yielding x≤ln(2)/ln(0.7)-9.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}2{(0.7)}^{x+9} & \ge 4 \\ {(0.7)}^{x+9} & \ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[(0.7)^{x+9}] & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ (x+9)\operatorname{ln}⁡0.7 & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡0.7$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+9 & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡0.7} \\ x & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡0.7}-9\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Solve the inequality 2(0.7)x+9≥4.

a
x≤ln⁡0.7ln⁡3+2
b
x≥3ln⁡0.7+2
c
x≤ln⁡2ln⁡0.7−9
d
x≥ln⁡2ln⁡0.7−3
e
x≤9ln⁡0.7−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Isolating the exponential term, we find 2(0.7)x+9≥4(0.7)x+9≥2.

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get ln⁡[(0.7)x+9]≥ln⁡2(x+9)ln⁡0.7≥ln⁡2.

Lastly, note that ln⁡0.7 is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality: x+9≤ln⁡2ln⁡0.7x≤ln⁡2ln⁡0.7−9

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality When the Base of the Exponential is Between Zero and One
content.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}2{(0.7)}^{x+9} & \ge 4 \\ {(0.7)}^{x+9} & \ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[(0.7)^{x+9}] & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ (x+9)\operatorname{ln}⁡0.7 & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡0.7$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+9 & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡0.7} \\ x & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡0.7}-9\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 7
?

Solve the inequality (0.84)x+5−20>0.

a
x<ln⁡(20)ln⁡(0.84)+5
b
x<ln⁡(0.84)ln⁡(20)+5
c
x>ln⁡(0.84)ln⁡(20)−5
d
x>ln⁡(20)ln⁡(0.84)−5
e
x<ln⁡(20)ln⁡(0.84)−5
Submit

decision.explanation: Add 20 to obtain (0.84)^{x+5}>20. Taking logarithms gives (x+5)ln(0.84)>ln(20). Since ln(0.84)<0, division reverses the inequality, so x<ln(20)/ln(0.84)-5.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}{(0.84)}^{x+5}-20 & >0 \\ {(0.84)}^{x+5} & >20.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[(0.84)^{x+5}] & >\operatorname{ln}⁡(20) \\ (x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.84) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡(20)\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.84)$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5 & <\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(20)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.84)} \\ x & <\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(20)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.84)}-5\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7

Solve the inequality (0.84)x+5−20>0.

a
x<ln⁡(20)ln⁡(0.84)+5
b
x<ln⁡(0.84)ln⁡(20)+5
c
x>ln⁡(0.84)ln⁡(20)−5
d
x>ln⁡(20)ln⁡(0.84)−5
e
x<ln⁡(20)ln⁡(0.84)−5
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Isolating the exponential term, we find

(0.84)x+5−20>0(0.84)x+5>20.

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

ln⁡[(0.84)x+5]>ln⁡(20)(x+5)ln⁡(0.84)>ln⁡(20)

Lastly, note that ln⁡(0.84) is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

x+5<ln⁡(20)ln⁡(0.84)x<ln⁡(20)ln⁡(0.84)−5

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms (x+5)ln(0.84)>ln(20). Since ln(0.84)<0, dividing reverses the inequality, giving x<ln(20)/ln(0.84)-5, which is option e.

content.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}{(0.84)}^{x+5}-20 & >0 \\ {(0.84)}^{x+5} & >20.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[(0.84)^{x+5}] & >\operatorname{ln}⁡(20) \\ (x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.84) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡(20)\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.84)$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5 & <\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(20)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.84)} \\ x & <\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(20)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.84)}-5\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8

Solve the inequality 34(0.54)x+3−2e≥e.

a
x≤ln⁡(0.54)ln⁡(2e)+1
b
x≥ln⁡(0.54)ln⁡(4e)+3
c
x≤ln⁡(4e)ln⁡(0.54)−3
d
x≤ln⁡(2e)ln⁡(0.54)−1
e
x≥ln⁡(4e)ln⁡(0.54)−3
Submit

decision.explanation: Add 2e and multiply by 4/3 to get (0.54)^{x+3}≥4e. Taking logarithms gives (x+3)ln(0.54)≥ln(4e). Since ln(0.54)<0, dividing reverses the inequality: x≤ln(4e)/ln(0.54)-3.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{(0.54)}^{x+3}-2e & \ge e \\ \frac{3}{4}{(0.54)}^{x+3} & \ge 3e \\ {(0.54)}^{x+3} & \ge 4e.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[(0.54)^{x+3}] & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡(4e) \\ (x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.54) & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡(4e)\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.54)$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3 & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4e)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.54)} \\ x & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4e)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.54)}-3\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Solve the inequality 34(0.54)x+3−2e≥e.

a
x≤ln⁡(0.54)ln⁡(2e)+1
b
x≥ln⁡(0.54)ln⁡(4e)+3
c
x≤ln⁡(4e)ln⁡(0.54)−3
d
x≤ln⁡(2e)ln⁡(0.54)−1
e
x≥ln⁡(4e)ln⁡(0.54)−3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Isolating the exponential term, we find 34(0.54)x+3−2e≥e34(0.54)x+3≥3e(0.54)x+3≥4e.

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get ln⁡[(0.54)x+3]≥ln⁡(4e)(x+3)ln⁡(0.54)≥ln⁡(4e)

Lastly, note that ln⁡(0.54) is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality: x+3≤ln⁡(4e)ln⁡(0.54)x≤ln⁡(4e)ln⁡(0.54)−3

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality When the Base of the Exponential is Between Zero and One
content.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{(0.54)}^{x+3}-2e & \ge e \\ \frac{3}{4}{(0.54)}^{x+3} & \ge 3e \\ {(0.54)}^{x+3} & \ge 4e.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[(0.54)^{x+3}] & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡(4e) \\ (x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.54) & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡(4e)\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.54)$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3 & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4e)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.54)} \\ x & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4e)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.54)}-3\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 9
?

Solve the inequality 5⋅(49)x<25.

a
x>ln⁡4−ln⁡9ln⁡5
b
x<ln⁡5ln⁡4+ln⁡9
c
x>ln⁡5ln⁡4+ln⁡9
d
x<ln⁡5ln⁡4−ln⁡9
e
x>ln⁡5ln⁡4−ln⁡9
Submit

decision.explanation: Divide by 5 to get (4/9)^x<5. Taking logarithms gives x(ln(4)-ln(9))<ln(5). Since ln(4)-ln(9)<0, dividing reverses the inequality, yielding x>ln(5)/(ln(4)-ln(9)).

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot {(\frac{4}{9})}^{x} & <25 \\ {(\frac{4}{9})}^{x} & <5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{4}{9})}^{x}] & <\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{9}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡9) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡5.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡9$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡9}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Solve the inequality 5⋅(49)x<25.

a
x>ln⁡4−ln⁡9ln⁡5
b
x<ln⁡5ln⁡4+ln⁡9
c
x>ln⁡5ln⁡4+ln⁡9
d
x<ln⁡5ln⁡4−ln⁡9
e
x>ln⁡5ln⁡4−ln⁡9
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Isolating the exponential term, we find

5⋅(49)x<25(49)x<5.

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

ln⁡[(49)x]<ln⁡5xln⁡(49)<ln⁡5x(ln⁡4−ln⁡9)<ln⁡5.

Lastly, note that ln⁡4−ln⁡9 is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

x>ln⁡5ln⁡4−ln⁡9

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms (4/9)^x<5, so x(ln(4)-ln(9))<ln(5). Since ln(4)-ln(9)<0, division reverses the inequality: x>ln(5)/(ln(4)-ln(9)), matching option e.

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality When the Base of the Exponential is Between Zero and One
content.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot {(\frac{4}{9})}^{x} & <25 \\ {(\frac{4}{9})}^{x} & <5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{4}{9})}^{x}] & <\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{9}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡9) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡5.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡9$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡9}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10

Solve the inequality (34)x+6+1≥2.

a
x≥ln⁡34+1
b
x≤3
c
x≤−6
d
x≥2
e
x≤ln⁡34−1

decision.explanation: Subtract 1 to get (3/4)^{x+6}≥1. Since 0<3/4<1, this requires x+6≤0, so x≤-6.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{3}{4})}^{x+6}+1 & \ge 2 \\ {(\frac{3}{4})}^{x+6} & \ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{3}{4})}^{x+6}] & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\ (x+6)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{4}) & \ge 0 \\ (x+6)(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡4) & \ge 0 \\ (x+6)(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+6) & \le \frac{0}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ x+6 & \le 0 \\ x & \le -6\end{aligned}
$$

Isolating the exponential term, we find (34)x+6+1≥2(34)x+6≥1.

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get ln⁡[(34)x+6]≥ln⁡1(x+6)ln⁡(34)≥0(x+6)(ln⁡3−ln⁡4)≥0(x+6)(ln⁡3−2ln⁡2)≥0.

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality When the Base of the Exponential is Between Zero and One
content.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{3}{4})}^{x+6}+1 & \ge 2 \\ {(\frac{3}{4})}^{x+6} & \ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{3}{4})}^{x+6}] & \ge \operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\ (x+6)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{4}) & \ge 0 \\ (x+6)(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡4) & \ge 0 \\ (x+6)(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+6) & \le \frac{0}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ x+6 & \le 0 \\ x & \le -6\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}4-{e}^{x+1} & >6 \\ -{e}^{x+1} & >2 \\ {e}^{x+1} & <-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Because a power of a positive number is always greater than $0,$ we must have

$$
{e}^{x+1}>0
$$

for all values of $x.$

Therefore, the inequality ${e}^{x+1}<-2$ has no solutions.

before.html:
Question 16
?

Solve the inequality 5⋅2x<32−x.

a
x<2ln⁡3−ln⁡5ln⁡2+ln⁡3
b
x>ln⁡5−2ln⁡3ln⁡2+ln⁡3
c
x<ln⁡3−ln⁡2ln⁡3+ln⁡5
d
x<ln⁡2−ln⁡32ln⁡3−ln⁡5
e
x>ln⁡5+2ln⁡3ln⁡2+ln⁡3
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking logarithms gives ln(5)+x ln(2)<(2-x)ln(3). Thus x(ln(2)+ln(3))<2ln(3)-ln(5). Dividing by the positive coefficient gives option a.

after.name: Question 16
after.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot {2}^{x} & <{3}^{2-x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(5\cdot {2}^{x}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2-x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2-x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡5+x\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & <(2-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡5+x\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & <2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡2+x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 & <2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & <2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x & <\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 16
?

Solve the inequality 5⋅2x<32−x.

a
x<2ln⁡3−ln⁡5ln⁡2+ln⁡3
b
x>ln⁡5−2ln⁡3ln⁡2+ln⁡3
c
x<ln⁡3−ln⁡2ln⁡3+ln⁡5
d
x<ln⁡2−ln⁡32ln⁡3−ln⁡5
e
x>ln⁡5+2ln⁡3ln⁡2+ln⁡3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

5⋅2x<32−xln⁡(5⋅2x)<ln⁡(32−x)ln⁡5+ln⁡(2x)<ln⁡(32−x)ln⁡5+xln⁡2<(2−x)ln⁡3ln⁡5+xln⁡2<2ln⁡3−xln⁡3xln⁡2+xln⁡3<2ln⁡3−ln⁡5x(ln⁡2+ln⁡3)<2ln⁡3−ln⁡5x<2ln⁡3−ln⁡5ln⁡2+ln⁡3

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality with Exponential Functions on Both Sides
content.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot {2}^{x} & <{3}^{2-x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(5\cdot {2}^{x}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2-x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2-x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡5+x\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & <(2-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡5+x\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & <2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡2+x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 & <2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & <2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x & <\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 18
?

Solve the inequality 3(15)x−2>32−3x.

a
x>3ln⁡3−ln⁡52ln⁡5
b
x>ln⁡3−2ln⁡53ln⁡3−ln⁡5
c
x<ln⁡3+2ln⁡53ln⁡3+ln⁡5
d
x<ln⁡3−2ln⁡53ln⁡3
e
x>ln⁡3+2ln⁡53ln⁡3+ln⁡5
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking logarithms gives ln(3)-(x-2)ln(5)>(2-3x)ln(3). Rearranging yields x(3ln(3)-ln(5))>ln(3)-2ln(5). Since 3ln(3)-ln(5)=ln(27/5)>0, division preserves the inequality, giving option b.

after.name: Question 18
after.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x-2} & >{3}^{2-3x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡[3{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x-2}] & >\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2-3x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x-2}] & >\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2-3x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(x-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{5}) & >(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(x-2)(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(x-2)(0-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(2-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ 3x\operatorname{ln}⁡3-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x(3\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 18

Solve the inequality 3(15)x−2>32−3x.

a
x>3ln⁡3−ln⁡52ln⁡5
b
x>ln⁡3−2ln⁡53ln⁡3−ln⁡5
c
x<ln⁡3+2ln⁡53ln⁡3+ln⁡5
d
x<ln⁡3−2ln⁡53ln⁡3
e
x>ln⁡3+2ln⁡53ln⁡3+ln⁡5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following: 3(15)x−2>32−3xln⁡[3(15)x−2]>ln⁡(32−3x)ln⁡3+ln⁡[(15)x−2]>ln⁡(32−3x)ln⁡3+(x−2)ln⁡(15)>(2−3x)ln⁡3ln⁡3+(x−2)(ln⁡1−ln⁡5)>(2−3x)ln⁡3ln⁡3+(x−2)(0−ln⁡5)>(2−3x)ln⁡3ln⁡3+(2−x)ln⁡5>(2−3x)ln⁡3ln⁡3+2ln⁡5−xln⁡5>2ln⁡3−3xln⁡33xln⁡3−xln⁡5>2ln⁡3−ln⁡3−2ln⁡5x(3ln⁡3−ln⁡5)>ln⁡3−2ln⁡5x>ln⁡3−2ln⁡53ln⁡3−ln⁡5

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality with Exponential Functions on Both Sides
content.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x-2} & >{3}^{2-3x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡[3{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x-2}] & >\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2-3x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x-2}] & >\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2-3x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(x-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{5}) & >(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(x-2)(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(x-2)(0-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(2-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ 3x\operatorname{ln}⁡3-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x(3\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 19
?

Solve the inequality 41−2x≤3⋅52−3x.

a
x≥2ln⁡5−ln⁡43ln⁡5+2ln⁡4
b
x≥ln⁡3−ln⁡43ln⁡5−2ln⁡4
c
x≤ln⁡3+ln⁡5−ln⁡4ln⁡5+2ln⁡4
d
x≤ln⁡3+2ln⁡5−ln⁡43ln⁡5−2ln⁡4
e
x≤2ln⁡5+ln⁡43ln⁡5−2ln⁡4
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking logarithms gives (1-2x)ln(4)≤ln(3)+(2-3x)ln(5). Rearranging gives x(3ln(5)-2ln(4))≤ln(3)+2ln(5)-ln(4). Since the coefficient is ln(125/16)>0, division preserves the inequality, giving option d.

after.name: Question 19
after.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{1-2x} & \le 3\cdot {5}^{2-3x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{1-2x}) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot {5}^{2-3x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{1-2x}) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{2-3x}) \\ (1-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡4-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ 3x\operatorname{ln}⁡5-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ x(3\operatorname{ln}⁡5-2\operatorname{ln}⁡4) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ x & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5-2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 19
?

Solve the inequality 41−2x≤3⋅52−3x.

a
x≥2ln⁡5−ln⁡43ln⁡5+2ln⁡4
b
x≥ln⁡3−ln⁡43ln⁡5−2ln⁡4
c
x≤ln⁡3+ln⁡5−ln⁡4ln⁡5+2ln⁡4
d
x≤ln⁡3+2ln⁡5−ln⁡43ln⁡5−2ln⁡4
e
x≤2ln⁡5+ln⁡43ln⁡5−2ln⁡4
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following: 41−2x≤3⋅52−3xln⁡(41−2x)≤ln⁡(3⋅52−3x)ln⁡(41−2x)≤ln⁡(3)+ln⁡(52−3x)(1−2x)ln⁡4≤ln⁡3+(2−3x)ln⁡5ln⁡4−2xln⁡4≤ln⁡3+2ln⁡5−3xln⁡53xln⁡5−2xln⁡4≤ln⁡3+2ln⁡5−ln⁡4x(3ln⁡5−2ln⁡4)≤ln⁡3+2ln⁡5−ln⁡4x≤ln⁡3+2ln⁡5−ln⁡43ln⁡5−2ln⁡4

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms x(3ln(5)-2ln(4))≤ln(3)+2ln(5)-ln(4). Since 3ln(5)-2ln(4)=ln(125/16)>0, division preserves ≤, giving option d.

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality with Exponential Functions on Both Sides
content.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{1-2x} & \le 3\cdot {5}^{2-3x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{1-2x}) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot {5}^{2-3x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{1-2x}) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{2-3x}) \\ (1-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡3+(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡4-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ 3x\operatorname{ln}⁡5-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ x(3\operatorname{ln}⁡5-2\operatorname{ln}⁡4) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ x & \le \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3+2\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5-2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20
?

Solve the inequality 7x+1>5x−1.

a
 x>ln⁡7ln⁡7+ln⁡5
b
x>−75
c
x>57
d
x>ln⁡7−ln⁡5
e
x>ln⁡5+ln⁡7ln⁡5−ln⁡7
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking logarithms gives (x+1)ln(7)>(x-1)ln(5), so x(ln(7)-ln(5))>-ln(5)-ln(7). Dividing by ln(7)-ln(5)>0 yields x>(ln(5)+ln(7))/(ln(5)-ln(7)), matching option e.

after.name: Question 20
after.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{x+1} & >{5}^{x-1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{x+1}) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x-1}) \\ (x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & >(x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡7+\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & >x\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡7-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >-\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >-\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ x & >-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\ x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality with Exponential Functions on Both Sides
content.worked_solution:
Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{x+1} & >{5}^{x-1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{x+1}) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x-1}) \\ (x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & >(x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡7+\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & >x\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡7-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >-\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >-\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ x & >-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\ x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{7}^{x+1} & >{5}^{x-1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{x+1}) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x-1}) \\ (x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & >(x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡7+\operatorname{ln}⁡7 & >x\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡7-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & >-\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & >-\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7 \\ x & >-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{\operatorname{ln}⁡7-\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\ x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\end{aligned}
$$
